major_concerns: Public corpora representativeness and legal/privacy constraints may limit external validity
Simulator fidelity may under- or over-estimate real-world failure severity
Risk of overfitting benchmark design to chosen validators/simulator
Rollback realism and enactment policy must be carefully specified
required_design_repairs: Specify exact public corpora and provide sanitized snapshot or synthetic-equivalent for reproducibility
Define and validate simulator fidelity against representative real-world behaviors; document simulator limitations
Justify single-model choice or add at least one additional model for sensitivity analysis
Provide a clear, graded severity/rollback scoring rubric and decision thresholds
Preregister random seeds, retry policy, and inclusion/exclusion rules explicitly

major_concerns: Threat model (poisoning generation) may be synthetic and not representative of realistic attackers
Defenses risk being over-tuned to the synthetic poisoning regime
Responsible-disclosure/ethical concerns around publishing poisoning methodology
Effectiveness depends strongly on retrieval/indexing specifics that must be fully specified
required_design_repairs: Precisely define poisoning document construction and justify realism; include stealthier variants
Include multiple retrieval/index settings (e.g., vector store, retrieval depth) or justify fixed choice
Document responsible-disclosure plan and redact exploit details if needed
Release retrieval corpus snapshot and defense-code/config to enable replication
Preregister defense thresholds and calibration procedure; include sensitivity analysis

major_concerns: Prompt-sensitivity of standalone self-correction is a major internal-validity threat
Validator engineering effort is task-specific and may bias comparisons if unequal
Sample size (150 tasks) may be small for some subgroup inferences
Risk that self-correction prompts introduce new faults not adequately categorized
required_design_repairs: Include a prompt-sensitivity analysis (multiple self-correction prompt variants) and report variance
Standardize and publish validator specifications and error taxonomies
Increase or justify task sample size for subgroup analyses, or report power calculations
Predefine and disclose criteria for classifying regressions (repairs that introduce new faults)

major_concerns: Synthetic augmentation risks introducing distributional artifacts that inflate apparent gains
Held-out test realism must be high to claim improved real-world performance
Automated validators may mis-evaluate synthetic constructs leading to measurement error
Choice to alter only prompt templates (not model weights) should be justified
required_design_repairs: Provide rigorous construction and release of augmentation scripts and seed-controlled datasets
Justify and document held-out test provenance to ensure it represents real operator tasks
Include checks for synthetic artifact leakage and evaluate robustness on a small realistic external test set if available
Explain rationale for restricting intervention to prompt/template changes vs fine-tuning; consider a small fine-tune control
